text: 📸 Encuentro bilateral México–Suiza — Palacio Nacional, 8 de julio de 2026

🇲🇽🌎 Switzerland is now Mexico's 6th-largest investor — $2.3 billion in 2025. "We are both pacifist countries, convinced of the peaceful resolution of disputes," Sheinbaum said. Amid global war and tariff threats, two sovereign nations chose to deepen cooperation. — Mexico–Switzerland bilateral, Palacio Nacional, July 8

🇲🇽🌎 Mexico and Switzerland move to modernize their free-trade agreement. "We have a trade agreement with Switzerland, and we agreed to keep working on it, to update it." Bilateral trade reached $4.272 billion in 2025. — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mexico–Switzerland bilateral, July 8

🇲🇽📈 22.7 million formal jobs — an all-time record. Mexico closed June 2026 with 22,779,704 formal jobs registered at IMSS, the highest in history, with the daily wage base up 6.4% to 669 pesos. — Zoé Robledo, IMSS director, mañanera, July 8

🇲🇽✊ First in the OECD for minimum-wage recovery. They said wages couldn't rise without killing jobs. Since 2018 the minimum wage more than doubled in real terms — and formal employment just hit a record. "Mexico is in first place in minimum-wage recovery." — Édgar Amador, Treasury Secretary, mañanera, July 8

🇲🇽🏭 Record foreign investment, record trade — the numbers the "failed state" narrative ignores. Mexico captured $41 billion in foreign direct investment, and Mexico–US trade hit a record $839 billion. "Mexico and the United States trade more than ever." — Édgar Amador, Treasury Secretary, mañanera, July 8

🇲🇽🌎 Mexico won't trade principle for protocol on Peru. "With Ecuador, we broke relations because they invaded our embassy. In the case of Peru, they broke relations. Why? Because we said President Castillo is imprisoned illegally." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, mañanera, July 8 Peru cut ties after Mexico refused to recognize Castillo's removal as legitimate.

🇲🇽🛢️ "I committed that there would be no gasolinazos, and we are keeping that promise." As the US–Iran conflict drives up global fuel prices, Sheinbaum said that without the government's measures a liter of gasoline would have hit 30 to 32 pesos. — President Claudia Sheinbaum, mañanera, July 8
